events.title: Augustus, First Roman Emperor, Dies
events.description: Augustus died at Nola, near Naples, at the age of 75. He had ruled Rome for more than four decades. His stepson Tiberius succeeded him.
events.significance: His death was the first test of imperial succession in Rome. The smooth handover to Tiberius showed that the empire he built could outlast its founder.

events.title: Afghanistan Gains Independence
events.description: Afghanistan was recognized as fully independent from Britain. This followed the short Third Anglo-Afghan War and ended British control over its foreign affairs.
events.significance: The date is still celebrated as Afghan Independence Day. It marked the country's return to full control of its own foreign policy.

events.title: German Referendum Consolidates Hitler's Power
events.description: German voters approved a referendum that merged the offices of chancellor and president. This formally made Adolf Hitler head of state as well as head of government.
events.significance: The vote removed one of the last constitutional checks on Hitler's rule. It cemented the dictatorship of Nazi Germany.

events.title: Sputnik 5 Carries Dogs Into Orbit and Back
events.description: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 5 with the dogs Belka and Strelka aboard, along with other small animals. They became the first creatures to orbit Earth and return alive.
events.significance: The flight showed that living beings could survive spaceflight and re-entry. It paved the way for Yuri Gagarin's first human spaceflight in 1961.

events.title: Comedian Groucho Marx Dies
events.description: Groucho Marx, the quick-witted, mustachioed star of the Marx Brothers films and the quiz show You Bet Your Life, died in Los Angeles at age 86.
events.significance: His rapid-fire wordplay and irreverent style influenced generations of comedians. His films remain classics of American comedy.
